title: Hazard Identification Checklist
subtitle: A field-level checklist for identifying workplace hazards before they cause harm
intro: Hazards that go unidentified cannot be controlled. This checklist gives inspectors a practical sequence for walking a site or area and systematically identifying physical, chemical, biological, ergonomic, and environmental hazards, along with the reporting process needed to act on them.

sections.title: Physical Hazards
items: Are moving machine parts, rotating equipment, or pinch points exposed to workers?
Are noise levels in the area within acceptable exposure limits?
Are vibration sources (hand tools, vehicles) identified and assessed?
Are sharp edges, protruding objects, or unguarded openings present in the work area?
Are extreme temperature sources (hot surfaces, cold storage) identified and controlled?

sections.title: Chemical Hazards
items: Are all chemicals on site correctly labelled and stored according to compatibility requirements?
Are safety data sheets available and accessible for all hazardous substances in use?
Are workers exposed to fumes, dust, or vapours without adequate ventilation or extraction?
Are spill containment measures in place for hazardous liquids?
Are incompatible chemicals segregated to prevent dangerous reactions?

sections.title: Biological Hazards
items: Are workers exposed to mould, bacteria, or biological waste without adequate controls?
Are sanitation facilities adequate and well maintained for the workforce size?
Is there a risk of exposure to bloodborne pathogens or contaminated sharps?
Are pest control measures in place where biological contamination risk exists?

sections.title: Ergonomic Hazards
items: Are workstations assessed for posture, reach, and repetitive strain risk?
Is manual handling of loads assessed for weight, frequency, and lifting technique?
Are workers exposed to prolonged awkward postures without job rotation or breaks?
Is seating, desk height, or equipment adjustable to fit the individual worker?

sections.title: Environmental Hazards
items: Is lighting adequate for the tasks being performed in the area?
Is ventilation sufficient to maintain safe air quality?
Are workers exposed to extreme weather conditions without adequate protection or shelter?
Are outdoor work areas assessed for lightning, flooding, or other seasonal hazards?

sections.title: Working at Height
items: Are edges, openings, and platforms at height fitted with guardrails or fall-arrest systems?
Is fall-arrest equipment inspected and within its certification date before use?
Are ladders and scaffolding inspected before use and free from visible defects?
Is access to elevated work areas restricted to authorised, trained personnel?

sections.title: Confined Spaces
items: Are confined spaces clearly identified, signed, and access-controlled?
Is atmospheric testing conducted before and during confined space entry?
Is a permit-to-work system in place for all confined space entries?
Is a trained attendant and rescue plan in place for every confined space entry?

sections.title: Housekeeping & Access
items: Are walkways, aisles, and emergency routes kept clear of obstructions?
Are spills cleaned up promptly and warning signs placed where needed?
Is waste and scrap material stored and disposed of in designated areas?
Are trailing cables, hoses, or cords identified as trip hazards and routed safely?

sections.title: Hazard Reporting Process
items: Is there a clear, accessible process for workers to report hazards they observe?
Are reported hazards logged, assessed, and assigned an owner for action?
Are workers given feedback on the outcome of hazards they reported?
Are hazard trends reviewed periodically to identify recurring or systemic risks?
Are high-risk hazards escalated for immediate control before the next shift begins?
